# Results — Study 904 (Shareholder-Yield + Quality)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
**buybacks add value only when they are REAL net share reductions at reasonable
valuations, so overlaying a QUALITY screen on a shareholder-yield sleeve should beat both
raw buybacks and the plain market on risk-adjusted terms** ("real buybacks, not dilution
theatre") — run live as a product race: **QSY = PKW + QUAL** (quality-screened
shareholder yield) vs **RAW = PKW** (raw buyback) vs **SPY**, all on monthly total
returns, all **excess of cash** (minus BIL). Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. Frozen as-of 2026-06-30 (the last
complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprint `6ab3e873ef9c`
(the 155×4 QSY-era monthly frame).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily auto-adjusted (**total-return, net-of-fee**) closes — PKW, QUAL, SPYD, SPY, BIL, BUYB (public, no key), cached as parquet under this study's own `_cache/` |
| Sleeves | **QSY** = equal-weight PKW + QUAL (buyback screen + quality overlay), **RAW** = PKW alone (unscreened buyback), both **monthly-rebalanced** to equal weight; **SPY** = plain market |
| Window | QSY-era common monthly sample **2013-08 → 2026-06 (155 months, 12.9 yrs)** — bound by QUAL's 2013-07 inception |
| Risk-free | **BIL** (1-3m T-bill ETF) — every Sharpe race is **excess-vs-excess**; BIL's monthly total return *is* the realized cash return (no ^IRX modelling) |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: rebalance to equal weight at each month-end (within-month drift only, no look-ahead). Costs = one-way spread × realized turnover; long-only, no shorts, no borrow; ETF fees already inside the net-of-fee tape (PKW 0.62%, QUAL 0.15%) |
| Statistics | excess-of-cash Sharpe race; Newey-West (HAC, 6-lag) *t* on the sleeve-minus-sleeve monthly spread; paired moving-block bootstrap CI on the Sharpe gap; max drawdown; calendar-year table; era cut (2020-01); 20-seed synthetic positive control |

**Survivorship / short-history — named on the Signal axis.** QUAL lists only 2013-07, so
the quality-screened race lives inside a single ~2013-2026 mostly-bull regime (one COVID
crash, one 2022 bear). These are surviving flagship products. **BUYB** (a standalone
buyback ETF) lists only **2026-05-07** (66 days) — **too young to race; named, not tested.**

## The race — excess-of-cash annualised stats (rf = BIL, 155 months)

| sleeve | CAGR | vol | excess Sharpe | max DD | $1 → |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **QSY** (PKW+QUAL) | 12.96% | 15.4% | **+0.764** | **−25.1%** | $4.83 |
| **RAW** (PKW) | 12.02% | 17.0% | +0.657 | −29.3% | $4.33 |
| **SPY** | 14.14% | 14.5% | **+0.874** | −23.9% | $5.52 |

The quality overlay lifts the raw buyback sleeve on every axis (higher Sharpe, lower vol,
a 4-point-shallower crash) — **but the plain market beat both.**

## Race 1 — does quality-screened shareholder yield BEAT THE MARKET? (QSY − SPY)

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| QSY − SPY | **−0.91 pp/yr** (−7.62 bps/mo) · HAC *t* = **−0.90** · one-sample *t* = −0.79 |
| excess Sharpe | QSY **+0.764** vs SPY **+0.874** → gap **−0.111** |
| bootstrap 95% CI (Sharpe gap) | **[−0.243, +0.013]** · P(gap<0) = **0.96** |
| RAW − SPY (for reference) | −1.51 pp/yr · Sharpe gap −0.217 · HAC *t* = −0.79 |

**No.** Both buyback sleeves *trailed* SPY. The market-beat is the **wrong sign**
(insignificantly): the bootstrap keeps the gap on the wrong side of zero (96% of draws
have QSY behind SPY). Owning plain SPY beat owning either buyback wrapper.

## Race 2 — does the QUALITY OVERLAY add value over raw buybacks? (QSY − RAW)

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| QSY − RAW | **+0.59 pp/yr** (+4.94 bps/mo) · HAC *t* = **+0.57** · one-sample *t* = +0.55 |
| excess Sharpe gap | **+0.106** |
| bootstrap 95% CI (Sharpe gap) | **[−0.013, +0.241]** · P(gap<0) = **0.04** |

**Directionally yes — but not certified.** The overlay lifts the Sharpe by **+0.106**, the
bootstrap is **96% positive** (only 4% of block-draws leave raw buyback ahead), and the
effect is positive in *both* eras — a genuine "real buybacks, not theatre" cleanup in the
right direction. Yet the HAC *t* is only **+0.57**: on 12.9 years of monthly data the
improvement does not clear the desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar, and the 95% CI grazes zero.

## Sub-periods — era cut (split 2020-01)

| race | early (2013-08→2019-12, n=77) | late (2020-01→2026-06, n=78) |
|---|--:|--:|
| **QSY − RAW** | gap +0.163 · +0.92 pp/yr · HAC *t* = **+1.12** | gap +0.073 · +0.27 pp/yr · HAC *t* = **+0.14** |
| **QSY − SPY** | gap −0.112 · −0.45 pp/yr · HAC *t* = −0.55 | gap −0.117 · −1.37 pp/yr · HAC *t* = −0.72 |

The quality-over-raw gap is positive in both halves (never significant); the market
shortfall is negative in both halves. Neither result certifies in a single era.

## Where the overlay helped — calendar-year total returns (%)

| year | QSY | RAW | SPY | note |
|---|--:|--:|--:|---|
| 2018 | −8.1 | −10.5 | −4.6 | quality overlay cushioned the Q4 selloff |
| 2019 | +34.0 | +34.1 | +31.2 | — |
| 2020 | **+12.8** | **+8.4** | +18.3 | overlay dodged the COVID junk-buyback names |
| 2021 | +29.8 | +32.6 | +28.7 | raw buyback's value tilt led the reflation |
| 2022 | **−15.4** | **−10.2** | −18.2 | rate shock rewarded raw buyback's cheapness |
| 2023 | +24.1 | +17.2 | +26.2 | quality led again |
| 2024 | +20.0 | +17.3 | +24.9 | — |
| 2025 | +15.3 | +17.9 | +17.7 | — |

The overlay's cushion is **crash-driven** (2018, 2020) — that is what shallows QSY's
drawdown to −25.1% vs raw buyback's −29.3%. The honest twist: in the **2022** rate shock
raw buyback's cheaper value tilt actually *beat* quality. The overlay cleans up the crash,
not every down year.

## Costs — a rounding error

| sleeve | turnover | cost drag (3 bps/side) | gross exSharpe → net |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| QSY (PKW+QUAL) | 0.76%/mo | **0.3 bps/yr** | +0.764 → +0.763 |
| RAW (PKW) | 0.32%/mo | 0.1 bps/yr | +0.657 → +0.657 |

Turnover is only the monthly drift of PKW/QUAL back to 50/50; raw buyback is a single ETF
(no rebalance). Costs move nothing — the verdict is a *significance* problem, not a
friction one. ETF fees are already inside the net-of-fee tape.

## Synthetic control — machinery proof (never market evidence)

A deterministic world where QSY = edge + 0.95·MKT + noise and RAW = 1.00·MKT + noise, both
excess-of-cash, with a **planted** quality-over-raw edge knob:

| planted edge | Sharpe gap | HAC *t* | 20-seed |t| ≥ 2 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **0%/yr (null)** | −0.090 (seed 904) | **−0.85** | **1/20** |
| **+3%/yr** | +20.46 | **+168** | 20/20 |

With zero planted edge the pipeline stays quiet (false-positive 1/20 ≈ nominal); a
planted +3%/yr lights up hugely. So a real quality-over-raw premium *would* have shown —
the market-beat one didn't, and the quality-over-raw one showed only weakly. *(A
faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of a stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The quality overlay genuinely **improves raw buybacks**: a shallower
  crash (**−25.1%** vs **−29.3%**) and an excess-Sharpe gap of **+0.106**, positive in
  *both* eras (+0.163 / +0.073) with the bootstrap **96% positive** (CI [−0.013, +0.241]).
  This is a real "real-buybacks-not-theatre" cleanup in the right direction — but it never
  clears the HAC bar (NW *t* = **+0.57**, no single era significant), and, decisively,
  **neither buyback sleeve beat plain SPY** (QSY −0.91 pp/yr, *t* = −0.90; RAW −1.51 pp/yr).
  The market-beat claim is the wrong sign; the quality-over-raw improvement is real but
  uncertified. Short single-regime tape (QUAL-bound to 2013). BUYB is too young to test.
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** The overlay is trivially buyable — cheap, liquid, long-only,
  a monthly rebalance whose cost drag is **0.3 bps/yr**, so nothing erases the QSY-over-RAW
  edge (not a Mirage). But there is **no significant premium to bank**: you buy a
  shallower-drawdown cleanup of raw buybacks, not a certified market-beating edge — and the
  whole complex trails SPY. Fragile is the honest stamp for a real-but-thin, uncertified
  tilt improvement.
- **"Beat the market?" — BUSTED.** Both PKW-based sleeves trailed plain SPY on CAGR and
  excess Sharpe over 12.9 years. The genuine (weak) win here is quality-**over-raw-buyback**,
  not buyback-**over-market**.
